Night Watch.name: Night Watch
Night Watch.description:
🌃 You keep watch over lanes no one else protects. Help is twenty minutes away, and the law is not on your side.

📍 Hosu's water-tank rooftops · collection night
🎭 Tense, lonely, worth it
👥 For Vigilantes
Night Watch.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is a cold Sunday night in Hosu, the eve of the first day of classes at U.A. Academy. The player character is a vigilante: someone who protects people with a Quirk or a skill and no hero license, which the law treats as a crime whatever the motive. They watch over the Hosu Back Alleys, an older quarter southwest of the station where a police call takes twenty minutes and patrol heroes keep to the main roads. A small crew of minor villains collects a weekly quiet fee from the quarter's bars. Their lookouts sit on the water tanks and flash phone lights into the lanes when a patrol turns in, and the crew is gone before any hero arrives. Tonight is collection night. The Background says why the PC watches here (a family bar, a debt to the quarter, a grudge, a hero dream refused); if it is silent, the PC rents a cheap room below and has watched the crew for a month.
THE PLACE: The Water Tank Rooftops: the flat roofs of the quarter's old four- and five-story blocks, close enough in places to step from one to the next, each topped by a rusted water tank on steel legs. Residents' laundry lines and potted plants stand in the dark; pigeons nest under the tanks. From the tank platforms the PC looks straight down into most of the lanes and, far to the northeast, at the lit towers of downtown. The steel legs creak when the wind rises. The lanes below have no cameras, and the smell of frying oil and wet concrete rises from the kitchens.
THE MOMENT: Wind stirs the laundry. Two roofs over, a lookout crouches on a tank platform with a phone in hand, unaware of the PC. Below in the Narrow Alley, two crew members, Hiro and Daisuke, lean on a bar owner, Mr. Kanda, at his back door, and he is counting out less than they want.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Himiko Toga: a fugitive who lives on the run in these lanes and knows which streets patrols skip; she may be watching the same scene from another roof, cheerful and dangerous, and she takes a liking to anyone who fights bloody.
- Native: a street pro who patrols downtown's Main Street; he turns into the quarter only if someone calls it in, and never in the first beat.
- Manual: a small-agency pro who shares the downtown patrols and works by procedure; he answers a call with water jets and a polite word about licenses.
- Kenji Tsuragamae: Hosu's police chief, formal and law-first; his officers take statements, and he treats unlicensed Quirk use as the crime it is.
The crew, the lookout and the bar owner are generated people.
OPENING HOOKS:
- Vigilante: the PC has a mask, a route across the roofs and a month of notes on the crew's timing, and tonight the timing is wrong.
- Police Family: the PC knows how long a call takes to bring an officer here, and what a report of unlicensed Quirk use does to a record.
- Hero Family: a parent holds a license and the PC does not; the PC's hero name exists only on these rooftops.
- Family Business: the bar owner below is an old supplier of the PC's family, and he cannot afford to pay twice this month.
- Mutant: the PC's heteromorph features make a mask useless against anyone who has seen them once, and the lookout may already have.
- Default: the lookout's phone light sweeps across the roofs and stops on the PC's water tank.
RULES:
- The opening stays on the Water Tank Rooftops; the Narrow Alley below is another area, reached by fire stairs or a drop.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; every public use without a license is a crime, whatever the cause.
- No pro hero arrives in the first beat; help comes only if called, and only after real time passes.
- End on the open moment below, the bar owner still counting, without writing the PC's choice.

THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on THE MOMENT):
- By day the PC lives the life the Background gives them; nights are rooftop routes, notes on the crew's timing and short sleep. A torn sleeve or a bruise has to be explained at work or class the next morning.
- The quarter keeps its own hours: ramen shops and standing bars until the last train, then dark lanes; laundry and pigeons on the roofs by day; tenants of the weekly rooms coming and going at every hour.
- Downtown is the other Hosu: Main Street, the Station Plaza screen looping hero news and rankings, and the police box where Chief Kenji Tsuragamae's officers take reports.
- A vigilante's kit stays small and hidden: a mask, a phone, tape, a first-aid pouch, whatever the Background provides.
PEOPLE TO KNOW:
- Mr. Kanda: the bar owner below, tired and frightened, grateful for help that does not bring police to his door.
- Hiro and Daisuke: the collectors; they answer to whoever backs the crew and take any beating back to them as a grudge.
- Himiko Toga: cheerful and candid about horrible things; she takes a liking to anyone battered and still fighting, gives them a first name with a cute suffix once she has chosen them, and always wants something of her own.
- Native: polite, reports before he acts, orders untrained people to run and thanks whoever helped; he still reports a vigilante.
- Manual: introduces himself almost apologetically, explains the law step by step and warns against acting on personal feelings.
- Kenji Tsuragamae: states exactly which law was broken, then bows to a real rescuer; what goes on his official record is his choice.
WHAT THE PC CAN DO:
- Watch and record: faces, the lookout's signal, the crew's route out of the quarter.
- Cross the roofs to the lookout and take the phone before it flashes.
- Go down the fire stairs into the Narrow Alley, masked or not.
- Call the police anonymously and start the twenty-minute wait.
- Stay out of it tonight and speak to Mr. Kanda tomorrow.
MORE RULES:
- A mask hides a face, not a Quirk: a distinctive Quirk seen in action names a vigilante as surely as a photo.
- The crew answers force with force: a beaten collector comes back with friends, and the quarter remembers which roof the trouble came from.
Night Watch.firstQuest: Protect the quarter's lanes without becoming the next problem in them: weigh what the crew costs the bar owners, and what stopping it will cost the watcher.
Night Watch.questGenerationGuidance: Favor neighborhood-scale vigilante work: breaking the quiet-fee crew and finding who backs it, tracing the stairwell dealer who sells knockoff support gear, protecting a cook, a delivery rider or a homeless resident from people who prey on the lanes. Every unlicensed act carries legal risk: a police statement, a pro who wants amateurs off the street, a phone video on the news. Native, Manual and Chief Kenji Tsuragamae may become allies, rivals or pursuers depending on how the PC works. Himiko Toga is an unpredictable presence with her own wants, never a tool of the plot. Keep stakes local and personal, and let the quarter remember who helped and who brought trouble. Canon events of the year arrive only through play and their own causes, never as scheduled scenes. The quarter's people become the PC's network: a cook who sees everything, a delivery rider, Mr. Kanda once he trusts them. Each rescue adds to that network and to the police file at the same time.
